title: Check yourself: declaring and invoking methods

questions.stem: Currency declares `static String symbol() { return "¤"; }`. Euro extends Currency and declares `static String symbol() { return "€"; }`. A price formatter runs `Currency c = new Euro(); System.out.println(c.symbol());`. What does it print?

options.text: €, since the call is resolved by the class of the object that c refers to
options.says: only an instance call looks at the object; a static call never does

options.text: €, since Euro's symbol() overrides the symbol() that Currency declares
options.says: a static method in a subclass hides the parent's, it does not override it; @Override on it does not compile

options.text: ¤, since the call is resolved by the type that c is declared with
options.says: the compiler binds a static call to the declared type of the expression left of the dot (invokestatic)

options.text: ¤, since a static method declared in a subclass is reachable only from code inside that subclass
options.says: Euro.symbol() is reachable anywhere through the name Euro or an expression of type Euro; the declared type decides

origin.section: An Instance Method Is Chosen by the Object; a Static Method by the Declared Type

questions.stem: Report has `String render() { return header() + body(); }` and `private String header() { return "REPORT"; }`. QuarterlyReport extends Report and declares `String header() { return "Q3 REPORT"; }`. Which header does `new QuarterlyReport().render()` start with?

options.text: Q3 REPORT, since render() runs on a QuarterlyReport object
options.says: the object's class picks only among overrides, and a private method has none

options.text: Q3 REPORT, since a subclass method with the same name and parameters takes the parent method's place
options.says: that holds for a method the subclass inherits; a private method is not inherited

options.text: REPORT, since the subclass's header() is a separate method that the call in render() never reaches
options.says: Report's own call keeps using its private method; @Override on the subclass method would not compile

options.text: REPORT, since render() is declared in Report, so every call made inside it runs Report's own methods
options.says: calls inside a class to an overridable instance method still run the object's override; only private and static are fixed

origin.section: A Private Method Is Never Overridden, So the Class's Own Calls Keep Using It

questions.stem: A payment service runs `ledger().append(nextEntryId(), format(tx));`. nextEntryId() takes the next number from a counter, and ledger() returns null while the ledger is read-only. During a read-only window the line throws NullPointerException. Which describes that line's run?

options.text: No entry id was taken, since the call fails on the null receiver before its arguments are evaluated
options.says: the receiver is checked for null only after every argument has been evaluated

options.text: No entry id was taken, since arguments are evaluated only once the method body starts
options.says: arguments are evaluated by the caller, before the method is entered

options.text: An entry id was taken and format(tx) ran, since both arguments are evaluated before the receiver is checked
options.says: the expression before the dot, then the arguments left to right, then the null check: the id is used up

options.text: An entry id was taken but format(tx) did not run, since evaluation stops after the first argument once the receiver is null
options.says: every argument is evaluated, left to right, before the null check on the receiver

origin.section: Every Argument Is Evaluated, Left to Right, Before the Method Runs

questions.stem: A recursive method walks a category tree 9,000 levels deep. In a staging test that has been running for an hour it works. In production, on the default stack and the same tree, it throws StackOverflowError for the first minutes after each deploy and works afterwards. Why?

options.text: The stack holds fewer frames just after start, since a method's frame is larger before the JIT compiles it
options.says: the limit is bytes of stack; interpreted frames are larger than compiled ones, so the same depth fails while the code is cold

options.text: The stack holds fewer frames just after start, since the JVM enlarges each thread's stack as the application warms up
options.says: a thread's stack size is fixed (1 MB by default, -Xss); what changes is the size of each frame

options.text: The limit is a fixed number of nested calls, so the production tree must be deeper than the one in staging
options.says: the limit is bytes, not calls; the same depth fails or succeeds depending on whether the method is compiled

options.text: The limit is a fixed number of nested calls, so production must be running more of these walks at once
options.says: each thread has its own stack, so other threads' calls don't count against this one

origin.section: Each Call Holds a Stack Frame Until It Returns, So Recursion Depth Is Limited by the Stack
